title: I made a website that automatically rigs and animates your hand drawings
author: DoodleMate
selftext:
(Screen capture not sped up or altered in any way.)  
  
For the past several months I've been building an app that lets children create expressive animated stories using their drawings. I thought this community would appreciate this particular piece of it. Give it an image of a well-silhouetted person-like figure and it'll rig it for realtime animation in about 15 seconds.

Don't take my word for it though. It's free and available on a browser (works on desktop and mobile). URL is the screen capture.

comments.author: Cool-Chemical-5629
comments.body:
>Give it an image of a well-silhouetted person-like figure

This is misleading. When you say "image", I imagine being able to upload actual image, but the reality is that you open a basic online editor which allows the user to draw the image by hand. That's a big difference and should be worded for what it really is. Other than that, it's a nice idea.

replies.author: DoodleMate
replies.body: It's not misleading. In the example video posted here I upload an actual image of a character drawn on real paper.

replies.author: Cool-Chemical-5629
replies.body:
https://preview.redd.it/ehddjrshltih1.png?width=531&format=png&auto=webp&s=95b1ad154326140157b060ee6cc058a349006672

Where do I click to do the same?

replies.author: DoodleMate
replies.body: ah- the image upload feature is age gated. if you're under the GDPR required age, it'll restrict you to in-app drawn images only since the images have to travel to our servers to be analyzed. Sorry :/

comments.author: EntryRadar
comments.body: What kind of AI does this use? Rigging feels like it’s probably super challenging

replies.author: DoodleMate
replies.body:
There a couple off the shelf models, one a few finetuned ones, and one newly architected one, plus a whole bunch of processing done on their outputs. 

I've got a Ph.D in graphics & animation and it's taken me a LONG time to get this working reliably so... yeah. super challenging :)

replies.author: Robdeprop
replies.body:
Props! Well done, looks amazing.  
A couple of years ago I got really far into doing all of this generatively without using AI models, to a point where it was all working, but yeah, when AI started coming around I was thinking, welp, should've waited a few more years, haha

replies.author: DoodleMate
replies.body: yeah? is anything you made public? would love to know more about how you tackled it a few years ago

replies.author: CryoNigiri_
replies.body: **What kind of infrastructure are you using to host the AI features, and roughly how much are you spending on it?**

comments.author: Short_Stable2397
comments.body: Very cool! I will definitely find the opportunity to use it in the future! Keep up the good work.

comments.author: TheFish77
comments.body: Pretty cool idea! I'm sure kids will have a blast with it.

comments.author: Livid_Shallot5701
comments.body: pretty good but the white outline kills my character

replies.author: DoodleMate
replies.body: That's a halo I add in post processing. I could make it optional with a toggle. What is it about white outline that kills it?

comments.author: MunchyCerealGuy
comments.body: Wow, this is really great. I was looking at your landing page and it looks like you're selling this to teachers? What's your goal for this technology? Asking because the silliness and whimsy of the dancing characters reminds me of Wombo's deepfake lipsync videos that had a super viral moment a few years ago among general consumers. What if you were able to interact with your doodled characters irl through a camera (I saw your github repo) in something like a TikTok filter game? Or make it multiplayer, where kids' characters can interact with each other - basically avatar driven experiences like Webkinz/Neopets/club penguin, but every avatar is something the kid drew. There's a seed of something really great and original here, congratulations!

replies.author: DoodleMate
replies.body:
Hey thanks for those positive thoughts! I agree that it feels like there’s something with legs here, and I’m trying to figure out what it is. Doing it solo though, so it takes time. I’ve built the rigging and animation tools to be performant and flexible- meaning that could already support the use cases you just mentioned. 

For now, I’m trying to build this into a full featured animation tool that’s still easy and accessible to everyone. I’m starting with teachers and kids because, if I can make something that they can use, then pretty much everyone else will be able to use it as well. It also just feels like a very wholesome and positive thing to be putting out into the world, which is what I want to do at this point in my career.
